text: - Batch of 2025 4 4 Placements 4 Infrastructure 4 Faculty 4 Crowd & Campus Life 4 Value for Money Four years heavenly life. Placements: During campus placement at my college 90% of students from my department got placed. The highest package offered is 80LPA and the average CTC is something around 12 to 13 LPA. Mass hiring companies for civil services are Godrej and ICICI Bank. 70% got internship. Top role offered was a Data Scientist Role. Infrastructure: Classroom is fully equipped with Wi-Fi and AC. The college has a central library where all kinds of books are available. The food and other facilities like gym culture room TV room everything is good. Time to time a special dinner is provided in the mess. All states' major festivals are celebrated in college. Faculty: Faculty members are quite outstanding and highly qualified in their subjects. They are helpful too like you can approach them regarding taking guidance related to internship or for referral for higher studies too. Semester examination difficulty level is moderate to slightly hard. Passing percentage totally depends on the professor mostly it is in the range of 35 to 40% percent. Other: I have chosen this course based on my JEE Advanced rank. I got a degree in civil engineering from IIT Bombay. Civil engineering is the fundamental discipline for infrastructure development of any country and this fascinates me to take this course. Many events and fest keep happening on campus, like Mood Indigo and Techfest. Reviewed on 12 Oct 2025 Read More S Shlok Nemani Integrated B.Tech. in Electrical Engineering + M.Tech. in Communication and Signal Processing - Batch of 2024 4.6 4 Placements 4 Infrastructure 5 Faculty 5 Crowd & Campus Life 5 Value for Money Great campus life, and you get to work with top professors in varied domains. Placements: Placements are really good in the EE branch, with opportunities from all the domains, including Core, Development, CSE, Consulting, and Finance, being thrown open to the students, so no dearth of opportunities. For sure 90% of students get placements and internships, and any student should least worry about those things. You get all the top recruiting MNCs here for the interviews. I feel EE is at a bit of a sweet spot compared to CSE in many regards. Infrastructure: While new residential buildings are coming up, the existing hostel infrastructure is a bit old, so there are some issues in that regard, and students should be mentally prepared for that. Academic infrastructure, including classrooms, labs, and a library, is at par with what students should expect from a good college. Faculty: It may feel like teaching is done in the same way as we go through the schools, since it's mostly the lectures and then you go through the exams (pen and paper), so it may feel like the same pattern but after 3rd year you get many opportunities to be more research oriented and curriculum becomes more project based. Course is enough for students to be industry-ready if they put in enough work. Other: EE as a department will be much better due to higher batch strength, as well as if people take integrated 5-year course, they do get an extra year to spend on the campus if they like.

Placements : IIT, Bombay is recognised all over India for its excellent placement record. According to official statistics for the placement season 2016-17 by the institute, jobs were offered to IITB students in engineering, IT, finance, consulting, analytics and education sectors. Around 84% of the B.Tech students (out of total B.Tech registered), and 82% dual degree students were placed. The average gross salary was 11.41 LPA, and the average CTC was 13 LPA. The highest offers ran into the range of 1-1.5 crores (unofficial figures). Almost all major companies, like Google, Microsoft, and prominent PSUs recruit from IITB. The placement season was coordinated by a dedicated placement cell, IIT Bombay. About 1000-1100 internship offers are made every year, from companies and universities in USA, UAE, Australia, Singapore, Europe, etc. Infrastructure : IIT Bombay infrastructure is a hit and miss. While the public buildings like lecture halls, auditoriums, open-air theatre, labs and indoor/outdoor sports grounds are world-class, the hostels especially the old ones, are in a bad state. Maintenance is done regularly, however, some old structures (as old as 1958) are almost beyond repair. Overall, the infrastructure can be classified as okay. Mess food is one of the weak points of the college. Almost no hostel mess offers delicious food, with the quality of food ranging from eatable to almost pathetic. This has initiated the construction of hostel canteens for each hostel. There is also a fine dining restaurant inside the campus that provides affordable good dishes. There is one hospital that is adequate for treatment of minor injuries and common diseases, however, for more specific or serious cases, it is recommended to visit a specialist outside the campus. Faculty : The faculty at IIT Bombay are prominent researchers in their fields, almost all of them being PhD holders from reputed universities in India and abroad. However, not all of them have a great style of teaching, so lectures can go from boring to pure fun depending on the type of professor. Research opportunities are quite enticing. The student to faculty ratio is also healthy. Most of the teachers teach using a combination of the blackboard and lecture PPT presentation, sometimes performing live experiments for more clarity. The first-year curriculum is mostly general and includes courses in physics, chemistry and math with one-two branch specific courses. The courses get almost completely branch specific in later years. With internships, students can get ample industry experience. Other : IIT Bombay conducts Asia's largest college cultural festival, Mood Indigo, Asia's largest college technical festival, Techfest, and Asia's largest entrepreneurship summit, Summit. Apart from this, there are numerous technical teams like AUV, IITB Racing, Innovation cell, Pratham (satellite), Rakshak (UAV), Team Shunya, etc., that participate and win competitions all around the world. There are 10-15 cultural clubs ranging from dance, dramatics, fine arts to writing, quizzing and modelling. Overall, the extracurricular activity scene is amazing in the campus.

To be precise December 1-18 is the first phase of placements. Most of the students get placed during this phase itself and phase 2 starts from January and companies come in scattered manner till April. Usually, there is 65-70% people placed every year. Don't be misguided by this number as many people even after registering for placements drop out of them for their other career plans like MBA, UPSC exam preparation, higher studies, start-ups, etc. Also, this percentage is a figures which takes into account all Bachelor, Master and Ph.D students. So, if you are in IIT Bombay and want to get placed, you will be placed with all probability. Highest salary is offered by Microsoft and Google and they offer $100,000/annum which when converted to INR is 70,00,000. Earlier it used to be Facebook which offered around INR 1.4 Crore. Minimum salary can be as as low as INR 3 Lakh, but almost all of them don't go for it, as it is too low for an IITian. Average salary varies from department to department in IIT Bombay highest average salary being INR 16 lakhs for chemistry and INR 15 lakhs for Computer science department. Then comes electrical with INR 12 lakhs .Detailed Placement stats can be viewed on http://placements.insightiitb.org/2015 . Almost all multinational companies visit IIT Bombay. AT Kearney, BCG, PwC, Strategy and Co., Bain and Co. are the top most consulting firms that come to IIT Bomaby and offer around INR 15 Lakh/annum and offer Associate consultant Job. FMCGs like Hindustan Unilever Ltd, P&G, ITC and Mendeloz foods are regular recruiters of interns but come occasionally to recruit undergraduates and offer around INR 18 Lakhs/annum and offer supply chain management profile. Almost all Wall street finance companies like Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank come for recruiting and offer around INR 14 Lakhs/annum and offer Analyst profile. PSUs like HPCL, ISRO also come for recruiting where ISRO offered INR 8 Lakh/annum and HPCL offered INR 12 Lakh/annum and offer Assistant Manager. Other than these around 250 companies come every year for recruiting. All above mentioned companies come for recruiting interns as well. Highest Stipend offered is 1.25 Lakh/month by P&G and people do unpaid internship for experience. Average Stipend is 10,000/month. Infrastructure : It will not be wrong to say that IIT Bombay has the best infrastructure in whole country. IIT Bombay is 550 acres lush green campus which rich flora and fauna, peaceful from the "Chaotic Mumbai". Only the academic area is equipped with Wi-Fi and you will get the fastest network speed that you might have never experienced(around 40Mbps).Almost all Classrooms are air-conditioned(exceptions being classrooms in respective department, which are very old), with even power plugs in case you required to use laptops in class(YES! Laptops are allowed in Class) and charge your mobile. Classrooms have different capacities ranging from 50-250, which are located in one building called Lecture Hall Complex, which is relatively new. Labs are not World-Class but good for Indian academic culture. Many equipment is old and experiments are not updated from time to time. Library has been renovated recently and is one of best in India. Fully air-conditioned, digital search of books, subscribed to monthly science journals are some features of library. Medical facilities is not that good and works fine for small injuries. Most of the time, students are referred to outside doctors for any serious medical issue. Sports and games culture in IITB is very rich and IITB has one of the best sports facilities. It has Football ground, Hockey ground, running tack, Olympic Size swimming pool, Gym, 2 synthetic basketball courts, 4 synthetic Volleyball court, 1 synthetic Kho-Kho pitch, 1 synthetic cricket Pitch, 2 Squash Courts, 5 wooden Badminton courts, 2 cement Basket ball Courts, 2 mud Volley ball courts and many Table tennis tables. If you are sports enthusiast, you will definitely find enough opportunities to prove yourself. Hostel rooms are very old and small. There is definitely a space constraint which is a problem and many people therefore prefer library to study. But newer hostels like H-15&16(for freshers only) are very spacious and much cleaner than old hostels and every student get a single room in their final yea . Food is mess is better in hostels where mess is rum by private caterers and worse in mess run by government caterers. As every hotel has a canteen, where people can order at cheaper rates, food is not at all a problem. Older hostels have been coming apart in terms of structure. Small mishaps have been happening here and there, so all hostels are going to be renovated in near future. Even Co-scholastic culture is very vibrant in IITB. Faculty : Faculty are very knowledgeable but not necessarily good teachers. If you utilize every opportunity that IITB offers, you can gain a lot of Knowledge. Professors are always there to help. Most of them prefer an appointment before meeting them(by mail or a call). but they do not mind if you show up at their office uninformed. They are definitely qualities and knowledgeable and always engage themselves in research in their specialized interests and open to students who want to help them in their research. Most of them use Powerpoint presentations as teaching method and transfer the presentations to us after each lecture. The faculty to student ratio is 1:10. Most of the industry exposure which you will get is only through your internship. Other than this, there are few to none industry trips organised in the entire curriculum. Course curriculum is very basic and rarely gets updated. But there is always flexibility in learning and any student can take any course from any department as additional learning and some courses are relatively new and bridges latest development in science. Undergraduate Project is not compulsory so many students get almost no flavor of real hand-on research other than small course projects which professors give. Academic pressure is normal,but sensitive people succumb to even such medium pressure due to job insecurity, parents' expectations, etc. Therefore, balancing ones academics is very important here and people who have not been able to do that have committed suicide (3-4 people in last 5 years). Other : Overall, IITB is definitely an engineering college that every student aspires to be in and worth fighting for. After getting into IITB, a person sees the world from a different perspective and has plethora of opportunities waiting for him. Be it academic, cultural, sports IITB satisfies every person.

Then comes electrical with INR 12 lakhs .Detailed Placement stats can be viewed on http://placements.insightiitb.org/2015 . Almost all multinational companies visit IIT Bombay. AT Kearney, BCG, PwC, Strategy and Co., Bain and Co. are the top most consulting firms that come to IIT Bomaby and offer around INR 15 Lakh/annum and offer Associate consultant Job. FMCGs like Hindustan Unilever Ltd, P&G, ITC and Mendeloz foods are regular recruiters of interns but come occasionally to recruit undergraduates and offer around INR 18 Lakhs/annum and offer supply chain management profile. Almost all Wall street finance companies like Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank come for recruiting and offer around INR 14 Lakhs/annum and offer Analyst profile. PSUs like HPCL, ISRO also come for recruiting where ISRO offered INR 8 Lakh/annum and HPCL offered INR 12 Lakh/annum and offer Assistant Manager. Other than these around 250 companies come every year for recruiting. All above mentioned companies come for recruiting interns as well. Highest Stipend offered is 1.25 Lakh/month by P&G and people do unpaid internship for experience. Average Stipend is 10,000/month. Infrastructure : It will not be wrong to say that IIT Bombay has the best infrastructure in whole country. IIT Bombay is 550 acres lush green campus which rich flora and fauna, peaceful from the "Chaotic Mumbai". Only the academic area is equipped with Wi-Fi and you will get the fastest network speed that you might have never experienced(around 40Mbps).Almost all Classrooms are air-conditioned(exceptions being classrooms in respective department, which are very old), with even power plugs in case you required to use laptops in class(YES! Laptops are allowed in Class) and charge your mobile. Classrooms have different capacities ranging from 50-250, which are located in one building called Lecture Hall Complex, which is relatively new. Labs are not World-Class but good for Indian academic culture. Many equipment is old and experiments are not updated from time to time. Library has been renovated recently and is one of best in India. Fully air-conditioned, digital search of books, subscribed to monthly science journals are some features of library. Medical facilities is not that good and works fine for small injuries. Most of the time, students are referred to outside doctors for any serious medical issue. Sports and games culture in IITB is very rich and IITB has one of the best sports facilities. It has Football ground, Hockey ground, running tack, Olympic Size swimming pool, Gym, 2 synthetic basketball courts, 4 synthetic Volleyball court, 1 synthetic Kho-Kho pitch, 1 synthetic cricket Pitch, 2 Squash Courts, 5 wooden Badminton courts, 2 cement Basket ball Courts, 2 mud Volley ball courts and many Table tennis tables. If you are sports enthusiast, you will definitely find enough opportunities to prove yourself. Hostel rooms are very old and small. There is definitely a space constraint which is a problem and many people therefore prefer library to study. But newer hostels like H-15&16(for freshers only) are very spacious and much cleaner than old hostels and every student get a single room in their final yea . Food is mess is better in hostels where mess is rum by private caterers and worse in mess run by government caterers. As every hotel has a canteen, where people can order at cheaper rates, food is not at all a problem. Older hostels have been coming apart in terms of structure. Small mishaps have been happening here and there, so all hostels are going to be renovated in near future. Even Co-scholastic culture is very vibrant in IITB. Faculty : Faculty are very knowledgeable but not necessarily good teachers. If you utilize every opportunity that IITB offers, you can gain a lot of Knowledge. Professors are always there to help. Most of them prefer an appointment before meeting them(by mail or a call). but they do not mind if you show up at their office uninformed. They are definitely qualities and knowledgeable and always engage themselves in research in their specialized interests and open to students who want to help them in their research. Most of them use Powerpoint presentations as teaching method and transfer the presentations to us after each lecture. The faculty to student ratio is 1:10. Most of the industry exposure which you will get is only through your internship. Other than this, there are few to none industry trips organised in the entire curriculum. Course curriculum is very basic and rarely gets updated. But there is always flexibility in learning and any student can take any course from any department as additional learning and some courses are relatively new and bridges latest development in science. Undergraduate Project is not compulsory so many students get almost no flavor of real hand-on research other than small course projects which professors give. Academic pressure is normal,but sensitive people succumb to even such medium pressure due to job insecurity, parents' expectations, etc. Therefore, balancing ones academics is very important here and people who have not been able to do that have committed suicide (3-4 people in last 5 years). Other : Overall, IITB is definitely an engineering college that every student aspires to be in and worth fighting for. After getting into IITB, a person sees the world from a different perspective and has plethora of opportunities waiting for him. Be it academic, cultural, sports IITB satisfies every person. Reviewed on 30 Apr 2020 Read More (5) 5 people found this helpful PS Parth Shettiwar B.Tech. in Electrical Engineering - Batch of 2021 3.8 4 Placements 3 Infrastructure 4 Faculty 5 Crowd & Campus Life 3 Value for Money Our college provides the worst hostel infrastructure, but it has a good curriculum. Placements : About 90% of the students from our course were placed with an average salary package of 13 LPA. The highest salary package offered is 1.5 crore per annum, while the lowest salary package offered is 4 LPA. Sony, Qualcomm and Tesla are some of the top companies which visit here for placements. About 80% of the students got internships in companies like Google, Microsoft, Adobe, Qualcomm, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, Samsung, etc. Infrastructure : In IIT Bombay, the infrastructure and facilities in classrooms and labs are world-class since all the classrooms were built recently. They all are equipped with Wi-Fi facility and very good. But the quality of food and hostel conditions are not good. Except for 2-3 hostels, rest of all hostels are very old, and it is not possible to stay in them. There will be litter everywhere, and hardly there are no good washroom facilities. However, there is a separate sports area on the campus, which is world-class with sports facilities ranging from squash, cricket, field track events, racket sports, basketball, hockey, volleyball. These all can be played in multiple courts wherever possible. Messes are in very bad in condition as every hostel has different caterer. As a thumb rule, there are private mess workers, and hence a private caterer provides better food than government mess caterer. IITB completely lacks medical facilities. Though there is a huge hospital, doctors are not useful. As for most of the diseases, they repeatedly offer the same type of medicines, which are not antibiotics but are just something like painkillers. There is no sort of professionalism in doctors. Most of the students here go to Hiranandani Hospital, which is located outside the campus, but they have to pay a hefty amount for the treatment. Faculty : Teachers are great in our course. Sometimes the course curriculum will not be perfectly designed for a subject, but teachers can easily clarify doubts when required. They also can be approached if any student wants to do research under them. I am not sure whether the course curriculum makes students industry-ready, but they can be research-ready. Professors use various techniques so that we have to do some sort of research sometimes or learn research aptitude. Other : I have chosen this course as I always like electrical and computer science. Due to my rank, I got the electrical engineering branch at IITB. In addition to electrical, I can also opt for computer science courses from time to time, and it is one of the best things at IITB. So, students can opt for any number of courses from any other department when required. Electrical engineering is quite an old department and quite organised. I suggest that our college should provide options for students to opt for particular courses available in the current list of subjects. We have to learn some specific courses mandatorily which they offer. It would be better if there is a little bit of flexibility in choosing some few courses for a semester like they can put an option to do power or digital courses in a semester. Our college organises Mood Indigo, which is one of the best cultural fests. In addition, It also organises techfest, i.e., technical festival, sports festival named Aavhan, a business festival named Cell Summit and social festival named Abhyuday. In addition, extra activities are organised by our department from time to time like trekking, trips, intra-departmental sports tournament, etc.

Reviewed on 18 May 2025 Read More P Pushkal Adlakha B.Tech. in Textile Technology - Batch of 2028 3.6 4 Placements 3 Infrastructure 2 Faculty 5 Crowd & Campus Life 4 Value for Money IIT Delhi is having boon and bane. Placements: I am currently in my first year, so I haven't experienced any placement or internship activities other than volunteering at OCS (Office of Career Services). I have just seen my seniors getting placements and internships, and I have inquired with them about it. As far as I know, most students who sit for placements get placed, with around 90% placement. In textile technology, most people do not go for core jobs but rather prefer tech jobs or consulting jobs, as core jobs are not much. Infrastructure: The infrastructure of the LHC (lecture hall complex), library, and Dogra Hall is quite appreciable. Classrooms in LHC are very good, fully air-conditioned, and have high-speed Wi-Fi. However, the hostel facilities are quite different from facilities in the institute. The hostel has triple-sharing rooms, which are quite congested. Buildings are very old, so maintenance is going on regularly. The mess is just awful. The food is barely bearable, and you can't trust it. I have to ask my parents for money to have good food that is eatable. When I am low on money, then only I eat from the mess. Faculty: I am not questioning teachers. They are quite knowledgeable of course and very much better than me, but students don’t understand what is being taught in class. They only go to classes due to 75% attendance. I feel that teachers in my coaching for JEE were not as qualified as professors here, but they knew how to teach, so students have an interest maintained. The curriculum has gone obsolete, it has no real-life applications, and one has to do an online course or learn from YouTube to get a job. The difficulty of exams matters to the professor. Other: At my rank in JEE Advanced, I was getting either Textile at IIT Delhi or Environmental at IIT Bombay. Because my hometown is Delhi, I chose IIT Delhi. Also, it is top-ranked among all IITs. I wish the course were designed to have some real-life applications. Now, it is just a thing to do, and you have nothing to learn from it. Fests are humongous, crazy, happening, and quite interesting. The extracurricular activities are many in number. One can do whatever he or she likes to dance, Spic Macay, and so whatnot. All sports are there, like hockey, aquatics, and water polo.

In addition, its proximity to universities such as Delhi University, JNU etc. Greatly increase the opportunities for students to participate in cultural events and competitions in these campuses as well. The fee is relatively modest considering the quality of the institute. There are several banks inside and near the campus and educational loans are provided without hassle. text: placements, average research. Placements : It is common knowledge that placements in IITs are great. IIT0Delhi, in fact, has better placements than most other IITs. The great location and proximity to the airport enable easy access for companies as well ( the location is a hindering issue for placements in IIT-KGP and IIT-K). People do get overseas offers of 1-1.5 crores but that is the case for very few people. Infrastructure : Infrastructure in IITD is better than most colleges in India, but it may be lacking behind some of the other IITs. Almost all of the campus has Wi-Fi. Classrooms are air-conditioned and the library is very well-stocked. There is a hospital on campus which can take care of day-to-day medical needs. Sports facilities for most games are available. Plenty of eating outlets are there on the campus which provide a variety of food items round the clock. Faculty : The faculty team in the college is highly variable i.e. some of the professors are extremely good and comparable to faculty members at Ivy League Schools in the US while some of the professors are not very proficient with the subject they are teaching. Placements : The placements were quite good of our senior batch but not as per the general trend. They were less as compared to previous years may be because of demonetisation or other reasons. More than 60% of the students got placed. The highest salary was around 50 lacs PA, the lowest was 9 Lacs PA and the average salary being 15 lacs p.a. Several companies visited the campus like Texas Instruments, Quallcom, Goldman Sachs, Samsung South Korea, Samsung Bengaluru, Samsung Delhi, Capital One, Citibank, ITC, American Express and D.E Shaw. Different roles were offered ranging from core/technical tasks to consulting and analyst, some were also offered jobs in the coding profile. 60% of the students got internship from our department. The highest stipend was 1.2 lacs INR, the lowest was 10,000 and the average was 30000 INR. Infrastructure : We enjoy the best facilities in the whole country and also on par with the best universities across the globe like Wi-Fi equipped classrooms, labs and hostel common rooms and hostel mess, 24*7 library and a computer center facility. We also have eating outlets open the whole night like tea halt and nescafe. There is a hospital with highly qualified doctors and students enjoy free appointments and medicines. There is a student activity center where we have indoor games like TT, badminton, pool, squash and a swimming pool. There are well-maintained stadiums for cricket, football and hockey and other athletic events. The class rooms have the best technology for teaching that include projectors, screens, electronic pens for screen, centralised cooling, etc. The labs also have the apparatus required to perform experiments and the professors keep a track of materials available and order new items if required. The quality of food is good and we get that at a lower price than is available outside. There are regular feedbacks and checks conducted by the BHM (Board for Hostel Management) to ensure the best quality. Hostel rooms are average with a fan. We have been allowed to buy our own cooler and keep it. During peak summers, they are not good to live in. Faculty : The professors here are of different nature. Some are very helpful and understand our problems while others want us to do whatever they say and become independent. On average, all of them will listen to your problems and respond. They teach very well and respond to your doubts, some teach using the blackboard while others prefer slides. Student to faculty ratio is about 30:1. We do get industry exposure during our internships or by doing independent projects under professors. The course curriculum is very effective, it was revised 4 years ago to groom the students in the overall personality development.

Review by a third-year student! Placements : The placements from our branch are mostly in non-core sectors. Generally, our branch has around 70% of the students getting jobs through campus placements. Companies that visit IIT Delhi are Mckinsey, Hindustan Unilever Limited, GlaxoSmithKline, Cipla, etc. The companies belong to the finance sector, consultancy sector, management sector and biotechnology sectors. Our branch has a unique approach in training a student for biotechnology, biochemical engineering, and bioinformatics professions at the same time. It is also a fact that biotechnology is a research-oriented branch. The scope of research in this field is immense. The toppers of branch usually go for higher studies in top universities in USA, UK, and Singapore. The highest salary offered was around 15 LPA last year and the average salary was around 6.5 LPA. I would say that it is a proper branch for pursuing research. Infrastructure : Our whole IIT Delhi campus is fully Wi-Fi equipped. The classrooms and laboratories are world-class. We have a lecture hall complex where our lectures, tutorials, and some labs are held which is estimated to be a 260 crore investment.We have a central public IIT Delhi Hospital which provides free treatment and consultancy to IIT Delhi students. We have a central library which has a diverse range of books. You will be enthralled by the range, quantity, and genres at IIT library. The students of IIT Delhi have access to all the books with a week long subscription or a semester long subscription. We have good quality playgrounds and courts for football, hockey, squash, cricket, and tennis. An Olympic-sized swimming pool adds to the wide range of sports a student can pursue. Faculty : The faculty at IIT Delhi has both good and bad professors. Owing to the reservation in teaching positions, some teachers are unsatisfactory. IIT Delhi has some great teachers in all departments which are leaders in their respective fields. The course curriculum is wonderful. A student has the flexibility to pursue courses from other departments. For example, a student interested in computational biology can opt for courses from mathematics and computing department. The teaching methods used vary while professors sometimes used PPT or they switch to a whiteboard to explain concepts. The exams conducted may of paper-based or computer-based. The student to faculty ratio varies according to the course. For instance, CVL100 course has one teacher and 450 students. TAs assist the professor in such cases. On the contrary BBL810 course has only 10 students. The average class size is around 80 students. Other : IIT Delhi is ranked 179 by QS rankings. It is the top University in India surpassing IISC Banglore and IIT Bombay. The selection in IIT Delhi is through IIT-JEE entrance exam. A student has to secure a good rank in IIT JEE Advance exam conducted annually. The rank must be above 4500 in JEE Advance to get a seat at IIT Delhi. The first-year courses are common for all undergraduate students irrespective of their department. IIT Delhi is located in the heart of New Delhi in Hauz Khas. The students have easy access to whole city owing to good metro network and Hauz Khas Metro station. I believe this location is one of the distinctive advantages that only IIT Delhi offers among all the IITs. Also, the students have the freedom to leave the campus and return at any time. The campus has various clubs and student societies such as Bloodconnect, NSS, AAIP, BSW, dance club, music club, PFC club, quizzing club, debating club, etc. which help in all-round development of the student.

The highest salary in my department (core) offered is around 20 lakhs(FMCG companies), lowest is around 5.5 lakhs and the average is around 8 lakhs. You can become sports personality, an actor/director, graphics designer, social entrepreneur or a civil servant which is completely different than what your department is expected you to become. IIT does not want you to become a good engineer but a good leader for the society.

Usually no fail grade is allowed for attendance shortage, However, one grade penalty is common. Placements : The placement session of IIT-Delhi begins after the 7th semester from 1st December. Most of the students who sit for the placements get placed during placement session. IIT-Delhi allows companies which offer a package of minimum 4.5 lakhs per annum. Companies like consulting firms, financing and management firms, start-ups, I-T firms and core companies of each branch come to offer a job to the students. The IT firms also offer jobs to the students who are not from the computer science departments but are interested in coding. The students are offered job profiles of Business Consultants, Management Consultants, Analysts, Product Managers, Software Engineers and even Assistant Professors. The companies also come to offer internships to students in the third year for different roles and the stipend can go up to six figures. Infrastructure : The infrastructure in IIT Delhi is pretty good. Wi-Fi is available in the institute area 24x7 and in the hostels, the Wi-Fi is available in a common area. All the classes of undergraduates are conducted in a newly built structure named as a lecture hall complex or LHC. The lab facilities are also pretty good but some of the equipment are outdated. The library has most of the books which are required for the courses but in limited numbers. IIT-Delhi has a hospital in the campus area which has a free consultation, free medicines, and doctors from AIIMS regularly visit there. The hospital remains open 24x7 and in the case of any emergency, the student is transferred to AIIMS. Sports facilities are available with all the sports and well-maintained grounds. SAC or student activity centre is available for all indoor sports and other extracurricular activities. Each hostel has a different facility for some of the sports like a badminton court, a table tennis facility etc. The hostel rooms are decent and a LAN facility is available in each room. The food in the hostel mess is average, not that good but there are several canteens available in the campus. The washrooms are also well-maintained in the hostels, but it also depends on the students. Faculty : All of the faculty members in IIT-Delhi are well-qualified. The minimum criteria for a faculty is PhD and a few other things. All the faculty members are very knowledgeable and are masters in their field but there is a very small number of them who could not communicate it to the students in an efficient way. Different professors have different teaching methods. Some of the professors focus more on the practical aspect of things and the others focus more on the theoretical aspects. There are theory classes and then one tutorial class or practical lab is conducted once every week to understand the course better. Almost all the professors are quite receptive to the doubts students ask during the lectures or after the class. The student-faculty ratio is a little poor as compared to other world-class universities and it is around 1 faculty for 20 students. But there are PhD students available to discuss the doubts if the professor is not available. The students can get an internship in the industries through their professors' help. The course curriculum in IIT Delhi is designed to make it understand the basics of each course to the student so that they can be able to pursue it further as per their interests. The students have to do a defined number of credits of humanities courses, some basic courses and some defined number of credits of other category courses which are not related to their core branch so that the students can get into another field if he/she is not interested in the core branch.

Reviewed on 13 Nov 2016 Read More AJ Arpit Jaiswal Integrated B.Tech. + M.Tech. in Mathematics and Computing - Batch of 2018 4 4 Placements 4 Infrastructure 3 Faculty 5 Crowd & Campus Life 4 Value for Money Life in IIT. Amazing infrastructure, rendezvous (biggest cultural fest in north). Hype in placement. Placements : Placement is awesome. Our placement season starts from 1 December and approximately more than 80% students get placed in the first week. Placement package varies from department to department like for CS, the highest goes to 1.30 crore given by Samsung, Korea whereas for mathematics and computing students it goes as high as 40 lakhs given by Word Quant. The average package for CS and mathematics and computing is approximately 18 and 15 lakhs and the lowest goes till 6 lakhs. IIT Delhi placement is high due to the startup culture. The majority of the students gets placed by IT companies like Samsung, Adobe, Amazon, Flipkart, Oracle, Infosys, Bidgely, Deutsche Bank etc. Internships in our college are necessary to get a degree. All the students had to do an internship or project. But a majority of the students, say 75% opt for internships for corporate experience and also for the stipend. Approximately, more than a half of the students gets internships through our placement cell but other students also get internships through their contacts and IIT brand value. This year, the highest stipend was given by DE shaw which was 2 lakhs. Average lies around 40 thousand. People from cs, electrical and mathematics and computing, everyone lands internships as the IT company used to come frequently. Infrastructure : Our campus has good infrastructure. Wi-Fi is provided in the academic area and recently, in every hostel. But hostel wifi has the range of around one room. Students use LAN for internet purposes which gives an average of 5 Mbps which is quite good. But the major drawback is that the LAN stops working after 1 am which is not appreciated by students. The college provides many opportunities for extra- curricular. We have hockey, cricket, football field, athletics track, 2 squash court, 6 lawn tennis court, snooker table, swimming pool, 2 badminton court and every hostel also gets two open badminton court. We have a hospital facility in which the doctors sit from 9 am to 8 pm and later, the emergency ward is functional. The hospital provides free medical and ambulance facility. Classrooms are fully air-conditioned and a wooden chair and desk are provided. Our new lecture hall complex has around 80-90 classes and the size of the class also varies. We have a wide range of books at our library which functions from 9 am to 9 pm on weekdays and on weekends, 9 am to 5 pm. This time is for taking books from the library. For studying purposes, it is open 24*7. Our library consists of mainly academic books. Literature art is not there. Labs are pretty good here. It is fully equipped with the latest technology and it is appreciated to work in labs. Recently, 4 new food outlets have been opened and one thing that I like here is cleanliness. Taste is decent but you cannot eat regularly as everything comes to be the same. But our hostel mess is bad. The result is so bad that in a hostel of 400 students, only around 200 take lunch, which is the worst meal of the day. But the other canteen is quite cheap and you can eat for 50 bucks. Hostel rooms are compact here. 2 freshers are provided 1 single room which was meant for one student. You can imagine 2 single beds on each wall and if you put a table in middle the there is no extra place left. Although, after the 2nd year you will be provided singe rooms. In my tenure, there was no such infrastructure issue. Faculty : Most of the faculty members are rude here. They don't take students lightly. According to them, if you have come at such premium college then you should not waste any time. Some of them expect to innovate in a course of 4 months in which first 2 months are lost in the introduction. Faculty members here are well educated and qualified for research but not for teaching. Teaching is an art which not everyone can do. I think IIT should provide compulsory training to the faculty here as they lack in the teaching aspect. Teaching is done on the blackboard, writing screen projector and slides. We have 2 minors and 1 major for each course and it is tightly packed. There is one exam every month. Our exam schedule is also tight. Many times, this results in 3 papers on a single day which is completely devastating. My department consists of 300 students and around 20 faculty members. So the ratio is 10:1. I have done an internship in Swiggy this year and it was completely a waste. I thought I will be applying my academics there but believe me, this is completely a waste. The only thing that matters is your skill to learn new things. Though my course turns out to be very exciting but it is completely a waste for people who want to do a job. Everyone thinks that our curriculum deals with finance and algorithmic trading but there is not a single course for this one. Other : Our cultural fest, Rendezvous is amazing. If you live in the NCR region, do come to our fest. The college also motivates our interest in extra-curriculum as there is a club for music, dance, drama, fine arts, debating, photography, literature, car making, economics, astronomy, robotics, and much more.

Reviewed on 5 Dec 2024 Read More (1) 1 person found this helpful B Budhyadeb Roy B.Tech. in Electrical Engineering - Batch of 2028 4.8 5 Placements 4 Infrastructure 5 Faculty 5 Crowd & Campus Life 5 Value for Money My first semester experience at IIT Delhi as an average student. Placements: In my opinion, IIT Delhi provides one of the best placements in India, and my branch has had a history of outstanding placements. Last year, my branch, Electrical Engineering, had an average package of 29.6 LPA and a median package of 24.5 LPA. The percentage of students placed was around 89%. It is pretty safe to say that if you are from the Electrical branch in IIT Delhi, you have an upper edge in the placement season. Infrastructure: As the college is old, there are many old hostels that have a kind of old infrastructure. If you are lucky, you may be given the new hostels, which have completely new infrastructure and can accommodate a huge number of students. Whereas, if you are unlucky like me, you may get an old hostel, where you will have to settle with two other roommates. Although the infrastructure in the old and new hostels is visibly different, the facilities provided are mostly the same among all hostels. You are provided with extremely fast Wi-Fi everywhere. The food quality is also decent; they provide a variety of foods (continuing both north and south Indian foods). Also, almost every hostel has its own night messes and juice shops, which provide you with many extra food options. There are also gyms, reading rooms, common rooms, visiting rooms, and a TV room in the hostels. There are also badminton and volleyball courts inside some hostels. The lecture hall has magnificent infrastructure and is huge in size. All the classrooms are air-conditioned. There are huge classrooms with a capacity of more than 300 students, and also smaller ones, each for their own purpose. There are well-equipped labs for each department inside the LHC itself. There is also a new LHC (West Academic Block) that will be soon operational. Faculty: The teaching faculty here are some of the best in the world. Each and every faculty member is a graduate of some prestigious international institution or another IIT. The professors are, no doubt, experts in their own field, but not every professor teaches the same way. Some professors teach with utmost interest and enthusiasm, while others just slide through some 2-year-old PPTs. You will also find most of the faculty members are very humble, and they do respond to students' doubts and questions. To be very honest, I personally find the first-year curriculum (which is the same for every B.Tech undergraduate, regardless of branch) not too relevant for everyone. In the first semester, I had to study a lot of mechanical and chemistry courses, which will hardly be of much use for my branch. In the second semester, I will study physics, electrical, and computer science courses, which again will not be of much use for most of the non-circuit branches. But the curriculum allows you to venture out into new areas, not only within your branch; you can explore many courses from any branch. And if you are passionate enough, you can also choose to minor in some other disciplines. The exams in IIT Delhi are a different monster. I personally remember sitting for the written test of a mechanical workshop course, and I couldn't believe the marking system. It was 30 marks, all multiple-choice questions with +1 mark for right answers and -0.5 for each wrong answer. The exams are very unpredictable and can often be very challenging, even for the best minds in the country, but the overall evaluation system is relatively consistent in most courses. The competition here is also cutthroat. If you thought getting into IITs is tough, surviving here is even tougher. Other: The campus life at IIT Delhi is really amazing. The cultural fest is one of the biggest in North India. The sports facilities are great. There are fields for each field sport, courts for racket sports, volleyball, etc. There is also Mittal Sports Complex and the Student Activity Centre (SAC), which contains playing areas for many sports. The inter-hostel sports competition (GC) is one of the legacies of IIT Delhi. Every hostel participates and competes to win the GC trophy, as it lifts the hostel's respect on campus. The campus overall has an amazing vibe. There is always some sort of sport or cultural competition going on. You will definitely not feel bored here.

Placements : The roles offered are mainly of software engineer and consultants. There were fewer core jobs offered in the placements last year. The highest salary was 1 crore INR per annum. To my knowledge, the lowest stipend is 5lakhs INR/ annum, but on an average, we can expect a salary of 20lakhs INR/annum. Infrastructure : The classrooms are air-conditioned and are always neatly maintained. The labs are equipped with all the equipment needed for the course so that the students don't face any problem. We can see a range of sports like cricket, football etc. We also have a hospital which is free for all the IITD students and staff. The library is air-conditioned and is available 24*7. The hostel rooms are small for the first year, but after that, you can get bigger rooms, this is due to an increase in the students every year. Faculty : The faculty are always friendly and will help with your doubts. If you are interested in the subject and have an idea to pursue further, they can assign a project on that. The student-faculty ratio is nearly 13:1. The industry exposure is less, but you can get what is done in the industry, in our fully equipped labs. Labs and classrooms are the best, fully air conditioned with almost all new equipments in them. Canteen will be opened for all the time with good food. Hostel rooms are just fine, not good and 3 people stay in a 2 seater room. Faculty : Faculty is awesome. Highly qualified, doing amazing research work, high level assignments are given for each subject to teach subject in the best possible manner. In each class there are around 50-150 students. Course curriculum is very good especially the right to choose subject of our own choice. Other : One of the best colleges in the country. A little hectic life, no doubt. But at the same, they bring out the best in you. A great place for all the students who wants to learn. If you ever get a chance to be part of this, then just go for it.

There is LAN internet in hostels too with 2 GB download limit per week but it stays shut during 1 to 6 AM. There is also high speed DC++ (local intranet).

Placements : DMS-IIT, Delhi placements are strong, touching the 100% mark easily both for the summers and the final placements. Being entirely student-driven body, the corporate relations and placements team, we invite some of the biggest names like Google, Amazon, Synergy Consulting, etc., in the business to our campus, who offer roles in finance, sales, marketing, operations, IT, analytics, consulting, etc., to our students. The average salary for the final placements stood at 16 LPA, whereas the summer internships garnered close to Rs. 97,000 for the 2 month internship period. The current 1st year and the 2nd year batches placements are ongoing, and a detailed report will be shared in the post completion. Infrastructure : We are housed in the same campus as IIT, Delhi and thus have access to all the amenities that are offered to the undergraduate students. They access to 24x7 high-speed internet in the campus and hostels, state of the art library with access to the major international journals, a dedicated sports arena for sports like lawn tennis, table tennis, swimming, badminton, cricket, football, field hockey, basketball, Volleyball, etc. We also have a dedicated student activity centre, which houses courts for squash, rooms for dancing and singing practice, and an amphitheatre. text: Reviewed on 4 Jul 2017 Read More (2) 2 people found this helpful NC Nikhil Chauhan B.Tech. in Materials Science and Engineering - Batch of 2015 4.6 4 Placements 5 Infrastructure 4 Faculty 5 Crowd & Campus Life 5 Value for Money Great college with a lot to learn. Best placements and infrastructure. Placements : The placements have been in accordance with the last few years. The first half of the batch got placed within 15 days with average CTC of 8 LPA, but the rest of the batch had to go on till the end of the graduation to secure a job. Most of the roles offered were in the Software segment as well as data analysts. Around 90% of the students went for internships either abroad or in different companies to gain experience. Infrastructure : IIT-Kanpur has one of the best infrastructures among the colleges in India. It has world-class sports equipment and the efficient staff members to help you through in any sports. The labs have all the necessary technical support required and the classrooms are very spacious. The hostels are provided with LAN ports in each room and the whole campus has an active Wi-Fi. The canteens are provided in each hostel and they operate till late night. There is an olympic-size swimming pool inside the campus and 3 indoor badminton courts to name a few. Faculty : Most of the faculty members are from the prestigious colleges across India and abroad with a PhD or higher qualification. A lot of them have an industrial experience as well which comes out to be very helpful for the education to be more practically-oriented. The student to faculty ratio was around 15 students per faculty which really helps everyone to interact with the professors even outside the lecture. Reviewed on 28 May 2017 Read More SY Shivam Yadav B.Tech. in Materials Science and Engineering - Batch of 2017 4.6 4 Placements 4 Infrastructure 5 Faculty 5 Crowd & Campus Life 5 Value for Money Offering freedom and overall development in 4 years, that's IIT Kanpur. Placements : Last year (2016), around 1200+ students registered for placement and around 700+ students got placed in different national as well as international companies (150+ companies) of different backgrounds for posts like data scientists, analyst, consultants, trainee engineers, etc. Big companies like Google, Microsoft, McKinsey, Credit Suisse, Opera, Tata Steel etc. visited the campus. Comparing to the year 2015, there is a decrease (around 9-10%) in the percentage of students placed. The highest placement of the year 2016 is 41 LPA and the lowest is around 4 LPA. Around 250-300 students, out of around 800 students, got internships in this sessions. The average stipend was around Rs. 15000, the highest is around 70-80k offered by ITC and other companies. I don't have any idea of the lowest stipend (in some cases, students works for zero stipend just to gain experience). Infrastructure : Almost 90-80% campus is Wi-Fi enabled and the Internet can be accessed by students after entering their login details. IITK has 19 lecture halls of average capacity around 300. The highest capacity (lecture hall 7) is around 500 and the lowest is around 170. PK Kelkar library is one of the biggest libraries available in Indian colleges. It has 3 floors and has thousands of old and new journals and excellent quality of digital material is available in the library's computer lab. Students are also notified about the weekly arrivals at the library. There is a health center hospital inside the campus where patients (students, faculty members, employees) are treated free of cost. Available games and sports facilities are of top-class. We have a main stadium, cricket pitch, practice pitches, hockey field, football field, 6 tennis courts, 50m Olympic size swimming pool, 4 basketball courts, indoor basketball court, table tennis facility, squash room, billiards room having 8 pool tables, badminton and volleyball courts, and apart from that, there 2 gyms and weightlifting facility. The labs are highly organized and equipped with the latest machines and equipment and are ideal for undergraduates as well as researchers (M. Tech, Ph.D.) pursuing higher studies in IITK. All the classrooms are fully air-conditioned and have digital facilities like high-quality projectors and audio system. We have canteens in each hostel (13 hostels and other buildings) and the quality of food in canteens is way better than a normal restaurant food at reasonable prices. There are other food outlets in the campus like CCD, Domino's, Kathi Rolls, Crown Burger, Urban Crave etc. Hostel rooms are good enough for 1 person equipped with LAN port ( unlimited Internet usage, line speed 1gbps) and daily room cleaning and maintenance available. I personally didn't feel any glitches whatsoever during my tenure. Faculty : IIT Kanpur's academics can be considered the toughest in India. The faculty members are highly experienced, skilled, and qualified. Most of them did their Ph.Ds and higher studies from world's top universities. Teaching methods used by professors includes computer slides, board work, lab experiments and sometimes models illustrations. We got industry exposure. The course curriculum was useful.

Reviewed on 22 May 2017 Read More AS Archit Sharma B.Tech. in Civil Engineering - Batch of 2018 4.4 4 Placements 5 Infrastructure 4 Faculty 5 Crowd & Campus Life 4 Value for Money An unforgettable journey of perfection. Placements : Placements have always been good at IIT Kanpur. More than 80% students get placed during the first phase of placement season. The average salary is between 12-20 lakhs per annum while the highest salary crosses 1 crore(but that is only in the CSE department). The internship opportunities are also a plenty. In our batch of 820 students, more than 600 people bagged the internship(research/technical) through the campus placement cell. The monthly stipend for the internship ranges from 10,000 to 2lakhs. Many tech giants visit the campus for both placements and internships (Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Facebook and Flipkart). The types of companies vary from startups to well-established corporates. Roles which are prominent are Analyst, Software Developer, consulting and financial services. Infrastructure : Our entire campus is Wi-Fi enabled. There are fully furnished classrooms with AC ducts. Labs are equipped with the latest instruments in the markets. Round the clock medical facilities are available at the health centre. It has one of the largest libraries in north India (in my entire time here I never needed to buy a book). Older hostel rooms are average while newer hostels have very good rooms (both single and double rooms). Canteens are quite decent in terms of quality but the mess is not. Sports facilities are excellent, A majority of the hostels has their own basketball, badminton and volleyball courts, while other sports (tennis, cricket, hockey, football) have separate facilities. Faculty : IIT-Kanpur has great professors who are masters in their field. IITK follows a three-tier teaching methodology which includes professors (who teach during the lecture hours), tutors (associate professors who conduct tutorial classes once a week) and teaching assistants (5th-year students who are there for the help of students). The student to faculty ratio is about 80:1. While direct industry visits are limited, a lot of projects are provided for students to learn on a first-hand basis. IITK can boast about being the most vigorous and competitive academic curriculum. The curriculum is very subject oriented and deals with practical aspects of engineering. Other : IIT-Kanpur is one of the very few colleges in India which has its own airstrip. Our gliding club organises monthly flights for the student community. The academic structure at IITK is very flexible with options like the branch change, minors in different fields and double majors available to the students. IITK has a relative grading policy rather than absolute grading policy. Our campus organises some of the largest inter-college technical and cultural fests (Techkriti and Antaragini). We also have a counselling service team who focuses on helping student facing any type of social issues and problems.

Reviewed on 20 Mar 2016 Read More NA nikita agrawal B.Tech. in Chemical Engineering - Batch of 2016 4.8 4 Placements 5 Infrastructure 5 Faculty 5 Crowd & Campus Life 5 Value for Money A university with one of the best facilities in India. Placements : The procedure for placement is pretty simple. The placement team is usually very cooperative to help you get into the company that you need. For my batch which sat for placements in December 2015, there was around 77% placement in the first phase (one month in December). The highest package for core in chemical engineering was around 20 LPA, the lowest was around 6.2 LPA. Along with a fair distribution of people in the low to high range, the average package goes to around 7.25 LPA, like every other year. Companies like ITC, HUL, Tata Steel, Reliance, Mu Sigma etc visited for core in chemical engineering. Usually, the students are offered a post of Associate Manager or Associate Trainee in these companies. Around 90% of the students in my batch got the internship from college. The stipend varied from as high as 75,000 per month to as low as nothing (unpaid), making an average of 25,000 per month. Infrastructure : IIT-K has world class facilities of all kinds from the Olympic-size swimming pool to the wooden basketball court, from supercomputers to the wind tunnel, from world-class labs to the airstrip, dancing, dramatics, literature, flying, etc. There is an awesome collection of books in the institute library, and the labs have all kind of equipment. The professors usually have enough budget to provide you all the facilities you need for your work. There is a big computer centre, spacious hostels, many food outlets, OAT etc. I never faced any kind of issue with the infrastructure or the canteen food quality, except for not having the mess food for long once I got bored with that. Faculty : The faculty team in our department is good in terms of their enthusiasm and research back ground. Although there were some professors who were more inclined towards research than lectures, you always get something to learn from everybody. There is a provision for all kind of teaching methods: slides, whiteboard, green board, poster notes, etc. But, the professors are really well-qualified and knowledgeable. The student to faculty ratio is around 1:20 for the bachelor batch. We had a course on the industrial process for which we had an industry visit to a nearby paper factory. The course curriculum was very well-planned, as at the end of four years of chemical engineering, we were able to see the applications of all that was taught in the design engineering course, which in one way gave meaning to everything we read before.

Also if a student, later on, decides to do a Mtech, he can opt for it in the 3rd year. Academics apart, IITK is one of the biggest and beautiful campuses in India with excellent infrastructure and all kinds of sports facilities. I don't feel there is anything which this college doesn't have, be it in terms of academics, sports, fun, crowd or anything.

IITK hosts three fests: The annual cultural fest is Antaragni. It attracts over 13000 visitors per day and features performances by well-known artists on a fiercely competitive national stage. The annual festival of technology and entrepreneurship is Techkriti. It is held in March. The annual sports festival is Udghosh. The campus is situated on the outskirts of Kanpur city but is well connected by roads. The nearest big station is Kanpur Central (CNB), at a distance of 14 km. The nearest airport is Kanpur (KNU), but CCS Lucknow Airport (LKO) is more convenient for more connectivity all over the country. There are several scholarships available for students. The placements for biotech in the core field were less. To my best knowledge, Biocon was the only core biotech company who hired from the college. Many students applied for research programs (approximately 30%) abroad, at places like USA, Germany etc, where there is a good scope for biotechnology. Biotech graduates got varied packages ranging from 8 lakhs to 20 lakhs (hired in a software company as a coder), and many students also received their internships from the campus interviews (30%). The highest pay packages offered went up to 1.2 lakhs (offered by FMCG companies like HUL, PNG, ITC), and the lowest according to me was Rs 20,000. Infrastructure : The infrastructure here is of the highest imaginable quality in any campus trough out the country. A cricket ground is present (Chemplast), where the first-class matches happen at regular intervals, it is also a place where international cricketers like Murali Vijay practice. We have T.T. tables across all the hostels, and the campus is also equipped with an Olympic-sized swimming pool. Also, a synthetic track is present here, and the hostel rooms are quite spacious and single accommodation is available for all the students. We have outlets such as CCD and Zaitoon which make the food inside IIT-M to be of great quality. Faculty : One of the best research programs across the country happens at IIT-M. Most of the professors are highly experienced in their fields and are also graduates from the same college. The faculty-student ratio is 1:40. Reviewed on 17 Nov 2016 Read More PG Prasanth Gollakota B.Tech. in Aerospace Engineering - Batch of 2018 4.2 4 Placements 5 Infrastructure 4 Faculty 3 Crowd & Campus Life 5 Value for Money Life in this college is awesome. It may not give you the best experience, but gives you the freedom. Placements : There are a number of companies that come for placements. If a job is what you are looking for, you will get one for sure, however, you may not get the job that you wish for unless you work hard throughout your 4 or 5 years for it. The issue here is, the job that you want or the company that you want to work for doesn't come for placements or doesn't prefer students from your branch even if they come. All the hype that IITians get high paying packages is true for only a few profiles in a few companies. Most of the jobs offer average pay and work is also mostly not your choice or not relevant to the courses you did. One more fact is that dual degrees get better job offers and higher average pay as compared to B.Tech degrees. But being a part of IIT obviously gives you an edge when you are applying for higher studies or jobs outside placements. Placements are one of the most overrated things. Placements are not the end of everything, there are so many other opportunities. For example, IIT Madras has a good incubation cell that encourages students to start up and get into business. And I need not stress about how a number of people opt for higher studies in foreign universities. Infrastructure : IIT Madras has all the basic facilities. LAN ports are available in your room, all labs, classrooms etc. There is no Wi-Fi facility for the whole institute. There are a few WiFi spots set up in few public spaces and labs, managed by responsible student bodies. The library is amazing, but hard to find the books, there will always be your classmate faster than you, who will come and borrow the books you need. There is a hospital in the institute which is free for all students, for any number of times to use the fees are already collected as a part of institute fees. The best part for curious engineers is there is a lab called Centre for Innovation, completely student run and free facility for students to come and work on innovative projects of their interest. Awesome robots and drones are made here. Faculty : The curriculum has changed from the batch admitted in 2015. It gives you the freedom to choose 50% elective courses, which we, admitted in 2014, wish we had. There will be courses which you won't miss even one class of. Not because of the 85% attendance rule (Yes, 85%), but because the professors are really amazing! There will be boring courses with the most boring professors who make you feel sleepy even after you have had a RedBull. There will be courses while you are doing them seem useless, but are really fundamental for the advanced courses you plan to take later on. Overall, the faculty here is very helpful, they'll offer you the best if you show interest. I rarely came across professors who don't try to help you. Other : One of the most important thing you need to be concerned about is the student body. First of all, there are two kinds of people; If you want to study well and get some good grades have a small circle of friends and leave the college, you needn't worry much about you peers. You'll get a good number of contacts, the profs will interact well with you. Life will be normal. But if you are involved in organizing events and working with a variety of people, you'll start making a number of acquaintances, you'll get into heated arguments, you will part of awesome events, lots of parties, lots and lots of meetings to make decisions, handle lots of money, pull so many night-outs just to get things right, everything besides trying to maintain a decent CGPA. Life is a lot crazier for these kind of students. There will be so many clubs you can be a part of, so many events you can host. Seriously, a lot of work can be done in your free time. Both have their downsides and none of the lifestyles is bad. It ultimately ends up as your choice and what you believe.

Placements : The placements can be divided into two categories: the first is core and the second is non-core. My seniors got the placements in different profiles in different companies here. For example, one of my seniors got placed in Flipkart for 22 lakhs per annum package in the coding profile, and another senior got placed in Goldman Sachs for 20 lakhs per annum in the finance profile. Generally, the average package of non-core profiles would be 10-12 lakhs per annum. Coming to the core, generally, you will not get much because four years of your core courses' study will not help much. With the exception of the CS branch, for the remaining branches, the average package offered would be around 6-7 lakhs. Since I am from the civil department, the core companies are L&T, Saint-Gobain, Shapoorji Pallonji, Schlumberger, and Shell. There are many other companies which have partial profiles of both core and non-core. Regarding internships, all the non-core companies come for taking the interns. Many people also get internships directly through professors, so the exact percent is not known. Infrastructure : The infrastructure here is really good compared to any other college outside. There is a 24x7 net facility, and the labs contain advanced equipment. But essentially speaking, the lab facilities vary from one department to another department. In IIT Madras, We have international-standard equipment in the lab for the civil engineering department. The newly started branches are growing day by day with their facilities in providing the sophisticated instruments. Our campus spreads over around 650 acres, and we have many places for eating. We have an IRCTC canteen which will operate 24x7, and we have other 5-6 canteens which give delicious food items at a decent cost. Coming to the medical facilities, we have our hospital which will be available 24x7. We have one of the best libraries in Asia as the central library is fully automated and in weekdays, it operates from 8 AM to 12 PM. On weekends, it will be from 8 AM to 5 PM. During exam time, it will be opened till 12 PM even on the weekends. Faculty : IITs are famous for their professors. Our faculty members are internationally reputed, but each professor's teaching style would be different. Some professors may not communicate well but if you personally ask doubts to them, they may explain brilliantly. Some professors stick to our old methods of chalk pieces and blackboard, while some other professors use presentations. But from many students' point of view, we consider the old method as the best. Our first-year curriculum makes you familiar with applications of our 12th standard physics, chemistry and maths in engineering. From the 2nd year onwards, the proper core courses start. You also have free electives in which you are allowed to take other department courses as well. The faculty-student ratio is around 1:15. Other : The main point about any IIT is the freedom. You have a lot of freedom in terms what you want to do and no one will force you. But it is up to you to make the best out of it. Freedom comes with responsibility, was the first line said by our director on the orientation session here.

Placements: For my course, I. e. B.Tech. In Civil Engineering, the following is the breakup: 1) 60% of the batch strength was placed in either non-core (Business, Analytics, consulting, finance) industry or IT (Software development, data Science) roles. 2) 10% of students who intended for core civil placements could convert into roles in a few Indian firms such as L&T, Shapoorji, etc. 3) 10% of students wanted to go for further higher studies and hence did not sit for placements. They were able to convert offers from highly renowned universities all across the globe, majorly from the US. 4) 10% of the batch did not get placed in the desired firm, sector, or industry and hence opted out from the official placements and tried externally via their own networks. Most of them have received at least 1 offer in hand in their desired area. Roles: 1) Non-core: Consulting and Finance are with the highest packages (averaging out at 18LPA for consult and 32LPA for finance) and most fierce competition 2) Non-core: Business Analyst, Growth and strategy, data analyst were the remaining roles with an average package of ~15LPA 3) IT- software: this year due to recession, the package averaged out at 30LPA, and the number of packages in total were also less than usual by almost ~20%. Mostly the firms were startups. 4) Core roles were offered by L&T, Tata, and Shapoorji. The average CTC was about ~8LPA. Infrastructure: Though the hostels are a bit old, but in terms of facilities you pretty much have everything that you would commonly ask for in a hostel or even for that matter in a PG: 1) Single/Double sharing room depending on your year in the college (usually single from second year onwards) 2) 1 Cot, 1 Table, 1 Chair, room with basic amenities like window and cupboard. 3) Washroom and bathroom are not attached to the room but are common for a wing of about 10-15 students, but are super clean and hygiene is maintained. 4) Gyms are available in most hostels or if not there is a central gym facility of international standards 5) Playground decent enough for a football match in every hostel. 6) Gymkhana having Olympic standard facilities for every sport you name: Badminton, squash, lawn tennis, table tennis, swimming, cricket, hockey, football, etc. ) 7) A common building in the middle of the academic and the student residential area is there for students and have almost all types of options ranging from south to north and east to west India. 8) Medical facilities: 24x7 hospital within the campus, free for students and staff (included in your fees, but practically free). Faculty: 1) Professors are the best in probably all of India, but you need to put in efforts in their course as well do some research in the areas of their interest to get the most out of them. They are helping but have a serious shortage of time to address all of student's queries, hence sometimes they tend to address only the more important ones (which means those that align with their research interests of course more). 2) The course curriculum starts from the very basic but does not cover the very modern stages in terms of construction management, materials, etc. Though there are some elective courses which cover these too, but they need to be chosen by the students based on their interests, and not many opt for these. They tend to opt for courses that are more related to computer Science such as AI/ML in the construction industry, etc. 3) The semester exams are pretty easy to pass if you study well (off course with a few exceptions), but to score a 10-pointer, you really need to be well-versed in every topic taught in the class. Other: This course has the following pros: 1) Compared to other courses offered at IIT Madras, this course enabled me to have a lot more free time (time apart from core academics) as the curriculum is designed in such as way, which gives the student a flexibility to explore other academic fields, other passions, and even other non-core business-related fields. 2) This dept. Is one of the oldest at IIT Madras and hence the Alumni base in all the sectors, be it academia, corporate, government. Is immense, and all of them are ready and willing to help you. You will probably find a stalwart in any sector you desire in this alum base and will be able to reach out via an email or LinkedIn message. That being said, there are a few cons as well: 1) The value of the course in itself is not much, and it is the value of the exposure, the peer group, and the network you develop here. But what you are actually learning in the classroom might not be useful to you in your life at a later point in time. 2) The number of students are very high (being one of the oldest dept. Here), hence if you do not really put in effort to learn, you might not really be learning something new here.

The average salary package offered for our branch was 15 LPA in 2019-2020. We get compulsory internships which are mostly paid. There are non-paid internships also. Infrastructure : The hostel facility is good enough here, and first-year students mostly get double or triple sharing rooms. Later, they will get single rooms. Faculty : The professors here are very knowledgeable and well qualified. The course will be a bit hectic and time-consuming. Apart from these, there are many clubs about robotics, astronomy, biotechnology, computer vision, analytics, dance, acting, etc. Which indulge in different types of activities and students can participate in them.
