Placements : When it comes to the placements in the institute, they were really good. The placement operation is handled by the placement team, by a group of students. They give us instructions, resume review sessions by seniors to make the placements happen. Almost 90% of the students sitting for placements get placed. These numbers include the students who do their M. Tech or MS or PhD as all of them will be sitting for the placements at the same time. Highest package offered in the institute was about 100000 USD per annum, this time, from the institute placement. I am not sure of any offers which came off-campus. Lowest salary is usually around 600000 INR per annum. Average usually is approximately 1200000-1500000 INR per annum. Some of the companies visited would be: Uber, Samsung, Microsoft, Rovigo, Schlumberger, HSBC, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, Citi, Cochin Shipyard Ltd., Amadasoft, Google, Airbus, Xerox, ITC, Hindustan Unilever Ltd., Wipro, DE Shaw, Cleanmax Solar, Wright Nanosystems, Reliance Industries, Vodafone, Caterpillar, Noodle Analytics, Indian Register of Shipping, Ernst&Young, Texas Instruments, Nvidia, Visa, American Express, Nomura, P&G, and many more. The roles offered were in the fields of the respective companies ie: finance, FMCGS, data analytics, Software Development, electrical engineering, Core roles in mechanical, naval architecture, civil, aeronautical, electrical etc. 70-80 percent of the students got internships including the research internships. Highest stipend offered was around 2.5 lambs per month, lowest was 6000 per month, and the average was around 25000 per month. Infrastructure : Wi-Fi is available in public spaces like the library, auditoria, etc. In the hostels, you don't have WiFi but LAN ports are there which offer you super fast internet connection where you can connect your own routers. Labs are all with state of the art facilities. Most of them are air-conditioned, with basic facilities on board. The library is fully air-conditioned and has WiFi. It has a computer centre which any student can use for academic purposes. There are a lot of books, both from academic and non-academic fields, like course books, novels, dramas, etc. Medical facilities are free on the campus for basic ailments, thanks to the health insurance. For serious issues, the patients may be moved to hospitals with a superior facility. Any kind of sport is open to all the students, which ranges from Frisbeeing to Football. Most classrooms are spacious, many of them are air-conditioned and others are not really that warm. All rooms have projectors and Internet connectivity to the main computer. There are a lot of canteens in the campus, most of them are open in the morning and remain open till midnight. Some remain open 24*7. Hostel rooms are shared for the first year and then you get single rooms. They have a fan and a lot of plug points which can be used for appliances which have a current rating of 5A or less. Faculty : The faculty is really good. You get to meet a free of the best minds in the country and in some cases, of the world, in different courses, projects and programs. Of course, there are really bad teachers too. All of the teachers are well qualified with an international reputation. On an average, the student-faculty ratio is about 50:1. The industry exposure is mandatory for the degree to be awarded to the student. Some make us think by ourself, where some make us memorise, and almost all the classes are interesting. The course content is decided by the faculty. The same course may feel different when taught by a different professor. Industry experience is mandatory for the degree to be awarded to the students. This should be done as an internship for a minimum of 40 days in the industry related to the department where the student is doing is B.Tech. The curriculum is mostly useful if you are into research and the core field. Most of the compulsory courses are not useful for moving into finance, analytics, consultancy etc. Other : You get to have exposure in any of the fields of your choice. Let it be finance, programming, arts, music, dramatics, choreo, technology, sports, speaking, writing, academics, quizzing, you name it; you will find a club related to it. And if you don't find one of your choice, you can create one of your own. There is no curfew for students in the campus. You can go out anytime and come back anytime you wish. Also, you can't use powered vehicles on the campus. There are provisions for differently abled students. It may not give you the best experience, but gives you the freedom. Placements : There are a number of companies that come for placements. If a job is what you are looking for, you will get one for sure, however, you may not get the job that you wish for unless you work hard throughout your 4 or 5 years for it. The issue here is, the job that you want or the company that you want to work for doesn't come for placements or doesn't prefer students from your branch even if they come. LAN ports are available in your room, all labs, classrooms etc. There is no Wi-Fi facility for the whole institute. There are a few WiFi spots set up in few public spaces and labs, managed by responsible student bodies. The library is amazing, but hard to find the books, there will always be your classmate faster than you, who will come and borrow the books you need. There is a hospital in the institute which is free for all students, for any number of times to use the fees are already collected as a part of institute fees. The best part for curious engineers is there is a lab called Centre for Innovation, completely student run and free facility for students to come and work on innovative projects of their interest. Awesome robots and drones are made here. Faculty : The curriculum has changed from the batch admitted in 2015. It gives you the freedom to choose 50% elective courses, which we, admitted in 2014, wish we had. There will be courses which you won't miss even one class of. Not because of the 85% attendance rule (Yes, 85%), but because the professors are really amazing! There will be boring courses with the most boring professors who make you feel sleepy even after you have had a RedBull. There will be courses while you are doing them seem useless, but are really fundamental for the advanced courses you plan to take later on. Overall, the faculty here is very helpful, they'll offer you the best if you show interest. I rarely came across professors who don't try to help you. Other : One of the most important thing you need to be concerned about is the student body. First of all, there are two kinds of people; If you want to study well and get some good grades have a small circle of friends and leave the college, you needn't worry much about you peers. You'll get a good number of contacts, the profs will interact well with you. Life will be normal. But if you are involved in organizing events and working with a variety of people, you'll start making a number of acquaintances, you'll get into heated arguments, you will part of awesome events, lots of parties, lots and lots of meetings to make decisions, handle lots of money, pull so many night-outs just to get things right, everything besides trying to maintain a decent CGPA. Life is a lot crazier for these kind of students. There will be so many clubs you can be a part of, so many events you can host. Seriously, a lot of work can be done in your free time. Both have their downsides and none of the lifestyles is bad. It ultimately ends up as your choice and what you believe.

Placements : The placements can be divided into two categories: the first is core and the second is non-core. My seniors got the placements in different profiles in different companies here. For example, one of my seniors got placed in Flipkart for 22 lakhs per annum package in the coding profile, and another senior got placed in Goldman Sachs for 20 lakhs per annum in the finance profile. Generally, the average package of non-core profiles would be 10-12 lakhs per annum. Coming to the core, generally, you will not get much because four years of your core courses' study will not help much. With the exception of the CS branch, for the remaining branches, the average package offered would be around 6-7 lakhs. Since I am from the civil department, the core companies are L&T, Saint-Gobain, Shapoorji Pallonji, Schlumberger, and Shell. There are many other companies which have partial profiles of both core and non-core. Regarding internships, all the non-core companies come for taking the interns. Many people also get internships directly through professors, so the exact percent is not known. Infrastructure : The infrastructure here is really good compared to any other college outside. There is a 24x7 net facility, and the labs contain advanced equipment. But essentially speaking, the lab facilities vary from one department to another department. In IIT Madras, We have international-standard equipment in the lab for the civil engineering department. The newly started branches are growing day by day with their facilities in providing the sophisticated instruments. Our campus spreads over around 650 acres, and we have many places for eating. We have an IRCTC canteen which will operate 24x7, and we have other 5-6 canteens which give delicious food items at a decent cost. Coming to the medical facilities, we have our hospital which will be available 24x7. We have one of the best libraries in Asia as the central library is fully automated and in weekdays, it operates from 8 AM to 12 PM. On weekends, it will be from 8 AM to 5 PM. During exam time, it will be opened till 12 PM even on the weekends. Faculty : IITs are famous for their professors. Our faculty members are internationally reputed, but each professor's teaching style would be different. Some professors may not communicate well but if you personally ask doubts to them, they may explain brilliantly. Some professors stick to our old methods of chalk pieces and blackboard, while some other professors use presentations. But from many students' point of view, we consider the old method as the best. Our first-year curriculum makes you familiar with applications of our 12th standard physics, chemistry and maths in engineering. From the 2nd year onwards, the proper core courses start. You also have free electives in which you are allowed to take other department courses as well. The faculty-student ratio is around 1:15. Other : The main point about any IIT is the freedom. You have a lot of freedom in terms what you want to do and no one will force you. But it is up to you to make the best out of it. Freedom comes with responsibility, was the first line said by our director on the orientation session here.
